children: NEW YORK, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- American Tungsten & Antimony Limited (

; OTCQB: ATALF) has demonstrated its U.S. mine-to-metal pathway with production of antimony ingot at the Del Sol Hydromet Refinery in Nevada, using material from the White Spar Antimony Mine in Yavapai County, Arizona.

The production of antimony ingot represents the first physical demonstration of the mine-to-metal pathway underpinning the company's US vertical integration strategy. The material processed produced antimony ingot without requiring new processing infrastructure or new permitting for the current campaign. More information is available here:

Casper Adson, Chief Executive Officer of American Tungsten & Antimony said, "This is a major milestone for us and a tangible demonstration of the potential strategic value of our proposed acquisition of the Del Sol plant. A mine-to-metal pathway for critical minerals on US soil is a key focus for the US and represents an important step toward our vision for a Critical Mineral Valley that brings US mining processing and downstream capabilities together in one integrated platform."

) is advancing critical mineral development in Tier-1 US jurisdictions with the strategic vision to become a vertically integrated, conflict-free supplier to Western economies. The company's flagship Antimony Canyon Project in Utah is one of the country's largest and highest-grade undeveloped antimony systems, historically mined but never subjected to modern exploration. The Tennessee Mountain Tungsten Project in Nevada and the Dutch Mountain Project in Utah further strengthen the company's critical minerals position, adding scale and diversification.
